answer: Reputation can grow like a vine: every identity traces its standing to established roots through real work delegations, and only the delta of earned trust flows down each branch. New identities start at zero influence and climb slowly; a clone forest from one actor shares few parent branches, exposing a shallow, wide thicket. Pruning snaps branches whose endorsers are un-established, and a dune of fake identities collapses because fake endorsements carry no weight. The attacker must earn real relationships per clone - full social cost per copy, while honest agents pay only patience.
